B01.key_observation: For every scanned supply the dry-reference top node becomes more negative, not wetter. At 1.02 KSAT h_top moves from -0.2 cm to about -0.223019 cm by 0.001 d and g=q_supply-q_cap moves from -0.02613 to -0.11478 cm/d. Capacity therefore moves away from the supply rather than toward a ponding threshold.
B01.mass_validity: The reported dry states are generally well inside the 1e-9 cm mass gate; the negative result is not explained by mass failure.

O14.key_observation: For every scanned supply the dry-reference top node also becomes more negative. At 1.02 KSAT h_top moves from -0.2 cm to about -0.879331 cm by 0.001 d and g moves from -0.01714 to -0.29457 cm/d. The capacity rises strongly instead of declining to the supply threshold.
O14.minor_solver_note: Some isolated early samples near 2e-5 d marginally miss the 1e-9 cm mass gate for lower supply fractions, but later mass-valid samples retain the same monotone drying/capacity-increase pattern; this does not create a hidden event bracket.

physical_interpretation: The frozen E3G initial profile [-0.2,-1.5,-5] cm is wetter at the top than below. Under the scanned sub-capacity supplies the top therefore drains/drys rather than following the classical rainfall-wetting trajectory in which infiltration capacity decreases toward a super-KSAT supply. The absence of a finite-time ponding bracket is a fixture-physics result, not a reason to increase forcing resolution or relax solver tolerances.
hard_guards: Do not add finer supply fractions to the same wet-top profile merely to manufacture an event.
Do not reinterpret B12/O13 immediate-R1 cases as finite-time events.
Choose future dry-profile candidates before execution and preserve this negative evidence.
Only mass-valid dry reference states may bracket a future finite-time event.
hard_nonclaims: No finite-time event localization is qualified.
No candidate event locator was tested.
